title: Device Mode State Machine
description: The Study Buddy has five modes (CLOCK, LISTENING, THINKING, SPEAKING, SETTINGS) and three buttons. Which mode the device is in decides what each button does. The rules are a transition table, and this MicroSim runs the same `Device` class as the chapter: a long press is 800 ms or more, releasing MODE before 0.2 s returns to CLOCK, and the volume starts at 40 and moves in steps of 10 between 0 and 100.

learningObjectives: The learner will use the device's state transition table to find the final mode and the final volume after 6 sequences of button events, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
prerequisites: device mode, state, event, transition, short press, long press, volume clamping (all defined in the sections above this block, with the table in the section "The State Machine").

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Why does a long press of UP in CLOCK not change the volume?
MODE did three different things in CLOCK, THINKING and SETTINGS. Which row of the table explains each?
Why is go() the right place to update the status indicator?
commonMisconceptions: (1) A button does the same thing in every mode. (2) Releasing MODE always sends the recording to the server. (3) A long press of UP in CLOCK also changes the volume.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all six sequences. Mastery is 5 of 6 correct (both mode and volume) on the first attempt.
